title: Black Rain Falls on Moscow After Huge Drone Attack Hits Oil Refinery!
summary: Have you ever seen black rain? People in Moscow did this week after a huge drone attack from Ukraine. Nearly 200 drones flew toward the Russian capital, and one hit a big oil refinery. The explosion sent thick black smoke into the sky, and later, people found oily black spots on cars, clothes, and the ground. One woman said her friend's jacket was "covered in black specks" and joked about watching if their hair falls out. Russia's defense ministry said it shot down almost 1,000 drones and four missiles across the country in one day. Fires broke out at the refinery, and a nearby shopping center also caught fire. Moscow's four airports were shut, and over 500 flights were canceled. Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, said the attack was a response to Russia's strike on Kyiv last week, which set a famous monastery on fire. "If Ukraine burns, your Moscow will burn too," he said. Russia's foreign minister promised more strikes on Ukraine. The war has been going on for over four years, and drone attacks on Moscow are becoming more common. Even with air defenses, some drones get through. For ordinary Russians, the war is now coming home.
why_it_matters: This shows that even people far from the front lines of a war can be affected if attacks reach their cities, and that wars can spill over into everyday life.

background_read: The war between Russia and Ukraine began in February 2022, and since then both countries have used drones to attack each other's cities and energy plants.
Volodymyr Zelensky (the president of Ukraine since 2019) often speaks about defending his country and has warned that attacks by Russia will be answered.
An oil refinery is a factory that processes crude oil into petrol and diesel; when it burns, it makes thick, black smoke that can mix with rain.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ukraine launched the drones; Moscow residents saw black rain; Russia's defense ministry and President Zelensky made statements
WHAT: Nearly 200 drones attacked Moscow, hitting an oil refinery and causing black rain, fires, and airport shutdowns
WHERE: Moscow, the capital city of Russia
WHY: Ukraine struck back after Russia bombed Kyiv and set a famous monastery on fire

perspectives.description: Ukrainians might see this as a strong response to protect their country and show Russia that they can strike back.
Ordinary Russians living in Moscow now feel the war firsthand, with danger and dirty air, which could make them unhappy with their government.
Experts might say that drone warfare changes conflicts because it is cheap and hard to stop, and could lead to more attacks on cities.
